standard.name: The Water System Management Standard, Part 1 - Asset Management

assetTypes.name: Water system
assetTypes.description: Collection of assets that work together as a system to collect, treat, store, and deliver water to users

assetTypes.name: Water facility
assetTypes.description: Physical location where specific functions are performed in the production, treatment, and delivery of water; the use of water facilities is optional and can be used to organize or locate the assets contained in large and complex treatment and distribution systems

assetTypes.name: Source
assetTypes.description: Location where a supply of water, such as a lake, river, spring, or groundwater aquifer, is abstracted for use in a distribution system

assetTypes.name: Pump
assetTypes.description: Mechanical or electromechanical device that increases the hydraulic head (pressure) of a fluid flowing through it

assetTypes.name: Tank
assetTypes.description: Structure or container used to hold water or other fluids

assetTypes.name: Power
assetTypes.description: Device that supplies electrical power for use by electrical equipment, such as a generator, solar power system, wind turbine, or connection to a power grid

assetTypes.name: Treatment
assetTypes.description: Equipment or process that improves the physical, chemical, biological, or aesthetic quality of water

assetTypes.name: Meter
assetTypes.description: Device for measuring the Flow rate of water through a pipe

assetTypes.name: Electrical
assetTypes.description: Any electrical or electronic device

assetTypes.name: Valve
assetTypes.description: Mechanical device designed to close off or regulate the flow of water

assetTypes.name: Hydrant
assetTypes.description: Device that provides the equipment needed to attach a fire hose to a water distribution network for use in extinguishing fires

assetTypes.name: Junction
assetTypes.description: Section of a piped network that joins two or more pipes or conduits

assetTypes.name: Sampling point
assetTypes.description: Location or access point in a water distribution network that allows for a water sample to be collected for testing

assetTypes.name: Sensor
assetTypes.description: Device that measures a physical condition or parameter of interest

assetTypes.name: Analyzer
assetTypes.description: Device that conducts periodic or continuous measurements of a water quality parameter

assetTypes.name: Structure
assetTypes.description: Anything that is constructed or built with a fixed location on the ground

assetTypes.name: Water point
assetTypes.description: Location or facility where users can access water

assetTypes.name: Other vertical
assetTypes.description: Any other type of vertical asset not defined elsewhere in this standard

assetTypes.name: Pipe
assetTypes.description: Conduit that carries water or other fluids from one location to another

assetTypes.name: Canal
assetTypes.description: Artificial open channel or waterway constructed for transporting water, connecting two or more bodies of water, or serving as a waterway

assetTypes.name: Reservoir
assetTypes.description: Impounded body of water or controlled lake in which water can be collected and stored

assetTypes.name: River/stream
assetTypes.description: Large stream of water that serves as the natural drainage

assetTypes.name: Aquifer
assetTypes.description: Geologic formation that is saturated and sufficiently permeable to transmit useful quantities of water to wells and springs

assetTypes.name: Spring
assetTypes.description: Concentrated discharge of groundwater appearing at the ground surface

assetTypes.name: Riparian zone
assetTypes.description: Banks or immediate border of a stream or river

assetTypes.name: Infiltration basin
assetTypes.description: Shallow pond or depression used to infiltrate stormwater or runoff through permeable soils into a groundwater aquifer

assetTypes.name: Forest
assetTypes.description: Land area characterized by woody vegetation greater than about 5 meters in height

assetTypes.name: Wetland
assetTypes.description: Area that is inundated or saturated by surface water or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support a vegetation adapted for life in saturated soil conditions; includes swamps, marshes, and bogs

assetTypes.name: Watershed
assetTypes.description: Area from which water drains and contributes to a particular stream or river

attributes.name: Type
attributes.description: Type of asset, according to the definitions in Section 5.5

attributes.name: Name
attributes.description: Name used by technical staff to refer to the asset; might be left blank for many lower level assets

attributes.name: Asset ID
attributes.description: Unique code used to identify a particular asset in the asset register (see Section 5.2 for further details)

attributes.name: Description
attributes.description: Additional information to help staff locate or identify an asset

attributes.name: Photo
attributes.description: Photo of the asset

attributes.name: Parent asset ID
attributes.description: Asset ID of the asset that is a parent to this asset (see Section 5.3 for further details)

attributes.name: Location
attributes.description: Geographic location of the asset on the surface of the Earth; may be a point, line, or polygon

attributes.name: Location precision
attributes.description: Estimated uncertainty in the geographic coordinates, expressed as a distance

attributes.name: Elevation
attributes.description: Height above the surface of a defined ellipsoid model of the earth’s surface, such as WGS84, or the local mean sea level; a consistent reference system should be used for all assets within a water system

attributes.name: Elevation precision
attributes.description: Estimated uncertainty in the measurement of the elevation

attributes.name: Administrative region
attributes.description: Name that describes the administrative geography of the location; multiple levels may be separated by commas starting with the most general area, for example: Region, District, Municipality

attributes.name: Coverage area
attributes.description: Geographical area where the water system or service provides coverage or is legally obligated to serve

attributes.name: Sector
attributes.description: Name for a sub-region of the coverage area that is defined by geography or the physical layout of the distribution network

attributes.name: Route
attributes.description: Name or number of the meter reading route, which defines those meters that are assigned to a particular staff member or team

attributes.name: Address
attributes.description: Physical address or postal address where the asset is located; in the case of piped connections, the address of the customer

attributes.name: Urban-rural classification
attributes.description: Degree of urbanization, as defined by national standards or the Degree of Urbanisation method (OECD 2021)

choices.name: Urban
choices.description: Cities or densely populated areas

choices.name: Peri urban
choices.description: Towns and semi-dense areas, suburbs, or peri urban areas surrounding cities

choices.name: Rural
choices.description: Regions with low population density

attributes.name: Community
attributes.description: Name of the community, town, or neighborhood where a water system or facility is located

attributes.name: Accessible by road
attributes.description: Asset can be accessed by vehicles using a nearby road

attributes.name: Perimeter fence or wall installed
attributes.description: Fence or wall exists to provide physical security for the asset

attributes.name: Level 1
attributes.description: Highest or most general level of categorization to which the asset belongs under the asset hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 2
attributes.description: Second highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 3
attributes.description: Third highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 4
attributes.description: Fourth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 5
attributes.description: Fifth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 6
attributes.description: Sixth highest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Level 7
attributes.description: Lowest level of hierarchy

attributes.name: Status
attributes.description: How the asset is currently being used or operated

choices.name: Active
choices.description: Asset is in use or ready to use

choices.name: Backup
choices.description: Asset is installed or available onsite to be used as a backup to other similar assets in case of maintenance or failure

choices.name: Not functional
choices.description: Asset is not currently operational due to a failure or maintenance problem

choices.name: Under construction
choices.description: Asset is not operational because it is under construction

choices.name: Decommissioned
choices.description: Asset is no longer in use because it is permanently out of service

choices.name: Disposed
choices.description: Asset has been sold, demolished, or relocated to a disposal site

attributes.name: Condition
attributes.description: The physical or structural integrity of the asset

choices.name: Excellent
choices.description: Designed to current standards, operable and well-maintained

choices.name: Good
choices.description: Showing some signs of minor wear and tear, with minimal impact on performance; or, operable and well-maintained but not designed to current standards

choices.name: Fair
choices.description: Structurally sound but some deterioration or damage that is beginning to impact performance or require more frequent maintenance

choices.name: Poor
choices.description: Functional but requires a high level of maintenance to continue operating or requires major rehabilitation or replacement

choices.name: Very poor
choices.description: Serious problems that impact performance or safety; major rehabilitation or replacement required in the short term

attributes.name: Functional status
attributes.description: Most recent observation of whether a water system or water point is working as designed

choices.name: Functional
choices.description: In good working condition and regularly providing water according to the specifications in the original design

choices.name: Partially functional
choices.description: Provides water on a regular basis (possibly in a reduced capacity) but repairs are needed due to some maintenance issue or change in water quality or availability

choices.name: Not functional
choices.description: No longer providing water on a regular basis; this could be due to maintenance issues, changes in water availability or quality, or problems with physical access

choices.name: Decommissioned
choices.description: Permanently taken out of service, abandoned, or could not be found

attributes.name: Current replacement cost (USD)
attributes.description: Cost (in US Dollars) that would be incurred to replace the asset at the current time; this value requires regular updating based on depreciation and current market conditions; also known as CRC

attributes.name: Expected useful life
attributes.description: Number of years that the asset is estimated to function after installation if it is well maintained; also known as EUL

attributes.name: Probability of failure
attributes.description: Measure of the likelihood of a failure happening at any point in time, based on an analysis of the potential failure modes of the asset

attributes.name: Consequence of failure
attributes.description: Measure of the direct and indirect costs of asset failure, which may include financial, environmental, and societal costs

attributes.name: Asset risk
attributes.description: Business or organizational risk of asset failure, usually calculated from the probability and consequence of failure

attributes.name: Original cost (USD)
attributes.description: Total price paid (in US Dollars) to initially acquire an asset

attributes.name: Current rehabilitation cost (USD)
attributes.description: Cost (in US Dollars) that would be incurred to rehabilitate the asset at the current time

attributes.name: Manufacturer
attributes.description: Name of the business that produced or sold the asset

attributes.name: Model
attributes.description: Manufacturer’s designation for the particular model of the asset

attributes.name: Serial number
attributes.description: Unique identifying number or code assigned to a particular asset by the manufacturer or vendor, usually stamped or printed on the asset

attributes.name: Additional technical details
attributes.description: Any other technical information about the asset that is not captured by the attributes of this standard

attributes.name: Installation date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the asset was installed or purchased, which begins the period of useful life

attributes.name: Installed by
attributes.description: Name of the company or organization that originally installed or purchased the system or facility

attributes.name: Funded by
attributes.description: Name of the funding authority, lender, or donor who funded the purchase of the system or facility

attributes.name: Rehabilitation date
attributes.description: Date of most recent work done to restore the asset to its original level of service and extend its life

attributes.name: Last service date
attributes.description: Date of most recent service or maintenance performed

attributes.name: Rehabilitated by
attributes.description: Name of the company or organization that performed the most recent rehabilitation of the asset

attributes.name: Service interval
attributes.description: Recommended interval at which service or routine maintenance should be performed on the asset

attributes.name: Upstream asset
attributes.description: Asset ID of the upstream asset that supplies water to this asset
attributes.applicability: Type: Pump, Tank, Treatment, Meter, Valve, Hydrant, Junction, Sampling point, Water point, Pipe

attributes.name: Nominal diameter
attributes.description: An approximate measurement of the internal diameter of a pipe, conduit, pump, or junction, which is used to classify according to standard sizes

attributes.name: Pipe length
attributes.description: Total length of pipe in a given section or run for use in hydraulic calculations and modeling

attributes.name: Material
attributes.description: Material of construction for pipes, junctions, valves, meters, and other liquid conduits
attributes.applicability: Type: Meter, Valve, Hydrant, Junction, Pipe

choices.name: Brass
choices.description: Metal alloy of copper, zinc, and usually some lead

choices.name: Bronze
choices.description: Copper-base metal alloy that may or may not include tin, lead, or other metals in small amounts

choices.name: Copper
choices.description: Reddish metallic element that is ductile and malleable

choices.name: Cast iron
choices.description: Heavy brittle alloy of iron, carbon, and silicon that can be cast in specific shapes and has the ability to withstand shocks

choices.name: Ductile iron
choices.description: Similar material to cast iron, but with the primary graphite in a nodular or spheroidal form, giving it increased strength and flexibility

choices.name: Stainless steel
choices.description: Chromium alloy steel that is resistant to rusting and corrosion

choices.name: Steel
choices.description: Iron-base alloy containing up to 2 percent carbon that is heat treated

choices.name: Galvanized steel
choices.description: Steel that has a zinc coating to protect from corrosion and rust

choices.name: PVC
choices.description: Polyvinyl chloride, a type of polymer frequently used in pipes and containers

choices.name: HDPE
choices.description: High-density polyethylene, a type of polymer used in low-pressure applications

choices.name: Plastic
choices.description: Any high molecular weight polymer material that can be extruded, molded, or drawn into various shapes and sizes; use this category for any plastics that are not PVC or HDPE

choices.name: Monel
choices.description: Nickel alloy, primarily composed of nickel and copper, with small amounts of iron, manganese, carbon, and silicon, which is corrosion resistant

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any material not otherwise defined in this section

attributes.name: Minor loss coefficient
attributes.description: Dimensionless coefficient that can be used to account for the head loss associated with turbulence in bends, junctions, meters, and valves

attributes.name: Roughness coefficient
attributes.description: Dimensionless coefficient used to account for friction losses in flowing pipes in either the Hazen-Williams or Darcy-Weisbach head loss equation

attributes.name: Primary contact name
attributes.description: Individual or office responsible for management or administration of the water system or water point

attributes.name: Primary contact position
attributes.description: Title or role in the organization of the primary contact

attributes.name: Primary contact phone number
attributes.description: Phone number of the primary contact

attributes.name: Secondary contact name
attributes.description: Additional individual who may be contacted if the primary contact is not available

attributes.name: Secondary contact position
attributes.description: Title or role of the secondary contact

attributes.name: Secondary contact phone number
attributes.description: Phone number of the secondary contact

attributes.name: Date updated
attributes.description: Calendar date of the most recent update made to any attribute

attributes.name: Date inspected
attributes.description: Calendar date of the most recent inspection or audit of the asset, as defined by organizational asset management policies

attributes.name: Alternate ID
attributes.description: Optional additional identification code or number that is used by other data systems or organizations to track the asset

attributes.name: Import code
attributes.description: Identification code for an asset that was assigned by an external database or asset management registry, used to maintain backwards traceability for assets that have been imported

attributes.name: Water system type
attributes.description: Categorization of the system as a distribution network or a point source

choices.name: Distribution network
choices.description: Water supply is distributed to multiple users via a network of pipes

choices.name: Point source
choices.description: Users access water at a single location

attributes.name: Network type
attributes.description: Categorization of piped networks as branching or grid style

choices.name: Branching
choices.description: Pipes begin from a central point and split off into segments that are not interconnected to each other

choices.name: Grid or mesh
choices.description: Pipes split off into segments that are interconnected to each other downstream

choices.name: Mixed
choices.description: Network has aspects of both branching and grid styles

attributes.name: Management type
attributes.description: Type of organization that manages the operations, maintenance, and finances of the water supply system

choices.name: Utility
choices.description: Organization created by government through legislative action or a private partnership or corporation with a legal mandate to provide water services to a designated area

choices.name: Local government
choices.description: Local or municipal government office or staff directly manage the system

choices.name: Water user association
choices.description: Community-based organization or cooperative group of water users (also known as water user committee, WASHCO, or community-based management)

choices.name: Water authority
choices.description: Government agency or regulatory body established for the purpose of managing water service provision

choices.name: Private
choices.description: Individual, partnership, or corporation that owns and operates a water supply system but does not have a legal mandate to provide services to all water users

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other management entity not described by the other choices

choices.name: No management
choices.description: No individual or organization can be identified that manages the system

attributes.name: Number of households in service area
attributes.description: Total number of households within the area that a service provider is legally mandated to offer services to

attributes.name: Number of households currently served
attributes.description: Number of households with a functional connection or currently able to receive service (includes households with inactive, intermittent, or cut off services, if service could be re-established)

attributes.name: System or network diagram
attributes.description: Photograph of a recent map or diagram showing the location of water supply and distribution infrastructure

attributes.name: Total production of system
attributes.description: Amount of water that the system is able to supply, within current resource and design constraints

choices.name: Intake
choices.description: Facility located at the head of a conduit into which water is diverted

choices.name: Well field
choices.description: Group of wells treated as a single entity for administrative, production, and treatment purposes

choices.name: Pumping station
choices.description: Structure containing pumps and related piping, valves, and other equipment for pumping water

choices.name: Distribution system
choices.description: Network of conduits and related equipment by which water is distributed to consumers

choices.name: Pipeline
choices.description: Collection of pipes and related equipment that are jointed to provide a conduit through which fluids flow

choices.name: Storage facility
choices.description: One or more tanks or storage reservoirs and related equipment used to maintain pressure and store water to accommodate intermittent periods of higher usage

choices.name: Treatment plant
choices.description: Facility or area that contains various treatment works, process areas, and other equipment necessary to improve the quality of water

choices.name: Process area
choices.description: Area or building, often contained within a treatment plant, where a specific water treatment process is carried out

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of water facility not defined in this section

attributes.name: Process area type
attributes.description: Optional label used to categorize process areas

attributes.name: Source type
attributes.description: Characterization of the source based on type of technology

choices.name: Intake
choices.description: Works or structures at the head of a conduit into which water is diverted

choices.name: Spring
choices.description: Concentrated discharge of groundwater appearing at the ground surface as a current of flowing water

choices.name: Borehole
choices.description: Deep hole with a small diameter that has been driven, bored, or drilled, in order to reach groundwater and constructed with casing or pipes to prevent collapse and contamination

choices.name: Dug well
choices.description: Shallow hole with a large diameter that is dug into the ground to reach groundwater

choices.name: Rainwater catchment
choices.description: System that collects rainwater from large surfaces, such as a roof or impermeable ground surface, so that it can be stored

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of source not otherwise defined in this section

attributes.name: Source meter installed
attributes.description: Meter is installed at the source to measure total flow

attributes.name: Water quality tested
attributes.description: Water quality testing has been performed at this source

attributes.name: Date of most recent sample
attributes.description: Calendar date of most recent water quality sampling at this source

attributes.name: Name of water body
attributes.description: Name of the water body supplying the source, if one exists

attributes.name: Source pressure
attributes.description: Pressure, or head, of the water leaving the source

attributes.name: Nominal flow
attributes.description: Typical or rated volumetric water flow rate that the source provides when operating as designed

attributes.name: Minimum flow
attributes.description: Minimum Flow rate rate that the source provides during the driest period of the year

attributes.name: Maximum flow
attributes.description: Maximum Flow rate rate that the source can accommodate during periods of high use or source water availability

attributes.name: Well depth
attributes.description: Depth below the ground surface to which the well was drilled, driven, or dug; in boreholes, this may differ from the casing depth

attributes.name: Well diameter
attributes.description: Inside diameter of the well; in boreholes, this is the drilled diameter, which will differ from the casing diameter

attributes.name: Static water level
attributes.description: Water level below the ground measured when no water is being taken from the aquifer by pumping

attributes.name: Dynamic water level
attributes.description: Water level below the ground measured when a pump is operating

attributes.name: Groundwater temperature
attributes.description: Temperature of groundwater in the aquifer or discharged by a pump

choices.name: Submersible pump
choices.description: Electrically powered pump designed to fit inside the well casing and to operate below the water level

choices.name: Hand pump
choices.description: Human-powered mechanical pump that uses suction or positive displacement to manually lift groundwater to the surface

choices.name: Rope and bucket
choices.description: Rope attached to a bucket on one end and a structure or winch on the surface to manually lift groundwater

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of pump not otherwise defined in this section, including centrifugal or positive displacement surface pumps, wind, and animal powered pumps

choices.name: None
choices.description: No pump is currently installed on the well

attributes.name: Apron installed
attributes.description: Apron is installed to protect the well from back-contamination by surface water and to channel drainage away from the well

attributes.name: Monitoring well
attributes.description: Well is primarily used for monitoring water levels and/or water quality rather than for water production

attributes.name: Spring box present
attributes.description: Protective brick, masonry, or concrete structure is installed around the spring so that water flows directly out through a pipe

attributes.name: Spring box length
attributes.description: Length of the longest side of the spring box, measured from the outside

attributes.name: Spring box width
attributes.description: Length of the shortest side of the spring box, measured from the outside

attributes.name: Spring box depth
attributes.description: Length of the vertical dimension of the spring box, measured from the outside

attributes.name: Overflow pipe present
attributes.description: Pipe is installed near the top of the spring box to allow water to exit when box is full

attributes.name: Drain pipe present
attributes.description: Pipe is installed near the bottom of the spring box to direct the flow from the spring

attributes.name: Casing diameter
attributes.description: Inside diameter of the well casing

attributes.name: Depth of casing
attributes.description: Depth below the ground to which the casing is installed; below this depth there would normally be a screen installed

attributes.name: Casing material
attributes.description: Well casing material

choices.name: Steel
choices.description: Iron-base alloy containing up to 2 percent carbon that is heat treated

choices.name: Stainless steel
choices.description: Chromium alloy steel that is resistant to rusting and corrosion

choices.name: PVC
choices.description: Polyvinyl chloride, a type of polymer frequently used in pipes and containers

choices.name: Plastic
choices.description: Any high molecular weight polymer material that can be extruded, molded, or drawn into various shapes and sizes; use this category for any plastics that are not PVC

choices.name: Concrete
choices.description: Mixture of cement and aggregate, usually reinforced with steel wire or rebar

choices.name: Fiberglass
choices.description: Reinforced plastic material composed of glass fibers embedded within a resin matrix

choices.name: Galvanized steel
choices.description: Steel that has a zinc coating to protect from corrosion and rust

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of casing material not described in this section

attributes.name: Screen length
attributes.description: Length of the well screen, which is a sleeve with slots, holes, gauze, or wire wrap installed below the casing to allow entry of water and prevent entry of sand or other large particles

attributes.name: Pump position
attributes.description: Depth below ground to the top of a submersible pump

attributes.name: Photo of well log
attributes.description: One or more photographs of the well log, or drilling log, which usually contains a record of the soil and rock formations (lithology) encountered during the drilling of the well; may also contain data on the casing and backfill used to reinforce the well

attributes.name: Pump type
attributes.description: Description of the pump mechanism or operating principle

choices.name: Submersible
choices.description: Electrically powered pump designed to fit inside the well casing and to operate below the water level

choices.name: Axial flow
choices.description: Fluid is accelerated in the direction of the flow axis by an impeller running inside a casing

choices.name: Centrifugal
choices.description: Fluid enters along the pump axis, is accelerated by an impeller, and exits at right angles to the shaft; also known as a radial flow pump

choices.name: Reciprocating
choices.description: Fluid is moved by one or more oscillating pistons or plungers

choices.name: Positive displacement
choices.description: Fluid is trapped and forced to move to the discharge side by a piston, gear, or rotary vane

choices.name: Hand pump
choices.description: Human-powered mechanical device that uses a suction or positive displacement pump, often connected to a lever via a rod or chain, to manually lift water

choices.name: Hydraulic ram
choices.description: Device that uses the water hammer effect to use some of the energy of inflowing water to lift a smaller volume of water

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other pump type not described in this section

attributes.name: Pump diameter
attributes.description: Maximum outer diameter of a submersible pump

attributes.name: Pump power rating
attributes.description: Power consumed by a pump operating under normal pressure and flow conditions, as defined by the manufacturer

attributes.name: Pump motor configuration
attributes.description: Whether the motor and pump should be tracked as a single asset or as separate assets; in cases where the motor is separate from pump, this generally means that motors are interchangeable between pumps of a similar design

choices.name: Integrated with pump
choices.description: Motor and pump should be treated as the same asset

choices.name: Separate from pump
choices.description: Motor should be treated as a separate asset from the pump

attributes.name: Pump motor voltage type
attributes.description: Type of electrical power required by the pump
attributes.applicability: Pump motor configuration: Integrated with pump

choices.name: Single phase AC
choices.description: Alternating current electrical system that uses two wires: one neutral wire and one phase wire in which the voltage rises to a peak in one direction and then reverses to a peak in the opposite direction

choices.name: Three phase AC
choices.description: Alternating current electrical system that uses four wires: one neutral wire and three phase wires in which the voltage rises to a peak and reverses direction at different times

choices.name: DC
choices.description: Direct current system in which current always flows in one direction and the voltage does not change over time

attributes.name: Pump motor voltage
attributes.description: Normal operating voltage of the pump, as recommended by the manufacturer
attributes.applicability: Pump motor configuration: Integrated with pump

attributes.name: Pump motor max current
attributes.description: Current drawn by the pump when operating at the maximum or full load power rating
attributes.applicability: Pump motor configuration: Integrated with pump

attributes.name: Pump motor max power
attributes.description: Maximum, or full load power rating of the pump, as recommended by the manufacturer
attributes.applicability: Pump motor configuration: Integrated with pump

attributes.name: Design flow
attributes.description: Flow rate of the pump required by the system design under normal operating conditions; should be within the acceptable flow range as defined by the pump curve

attributes.name: Design head
attributes.description: Head, or pressure, shown on the pump curve at the design flow rate

attributes.name: Maximum flow (Q-max)
attributes.description: Maximum possible flow rate shown on the pump curve

attributes.name: Head at maximum flow (H-min)
attributes.description: Total head, or pressure, that corresponds to the maximum flow rate on the pump curve; also referred to as the minimum head

attributes.name: Minimum flow (Q-min)
attributes.description: Minimum possible flow rate shown on the pump curve

attributes.name: Head at minimum flow (H-Max)
attributes.description: Total head, or pressure, that corresponds to the minimum flow rate on the pump curve; also referred to as the maximum head

attributes.name: NPSH-R
attributes.description: Net positive suction head required (or minimum) by the suction side of the pump in order to prevent cavitation and evaporation (flashing)

attributes.name: Tank type
attributes.description: Characterization of the tank design

choices.name: Elevated
choices.description: Located on and supported by a tower; also referred to as an overhead tank

choices.name: Above ground
choices.description: Constructed or permanently installed on top of the ground surface

choices.name: Underground
choices.description: Constructed or permanently installed partially or completely underground; also referred to as an in-ground tank

choices.name: Break pressure
choices.description: Tank used for hydraulic isolation and surge protection installed in a pressurized system where the water surface is exposed to atmospheric pressure

choices.name: Portable
choices.description: Tank which can be moved from place to place; could be installed above or below ground

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other tank design not otherwise described in this section

attributes.name: Tank material

choices.name: PVC

choices.name: Plastic

choices.name: Concrete

choices.name: Aluminum
choices.description: Lightweight metal composed mainly of elemental aluminum that may be alloyed with other elements

choices.name: Steel

choices.name: Composite

choices.name: Fiberglass
choices.description: Reinforced plastic material composed of glass fibers embedded within a resin matrix

choices.name: Masonry
choices.description: Brick, stone, or concrete blocks that are bound together with mortar

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of tank construction not described in this section

attributes.name: Tank volume
attributes.description: Useful volume of the tank which can be supplied from the minimum to the maximum water levels.

attributes.name: Tank shape

choices.name: Cylindrical
choices.description: Circular base with vertical sides

choices.name: Rectangular
choices.description: Square or rectangular base with vertical sides

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other shape not otherwise described in the section

attributes.name: Tank diameter
attributes.description: Diameter of the base of a cylindrical tank

attributes.name: Tank height

attributes.name: Tank length

attributes.name: Tank width

attributes.name: Height of tank bottom
attributes.description: Distance from the ground level to the bottom of the inside of the tank; negative values are used for depths below the ground

attributes.name: Minimum water level
attributes.description: Minimum water level allowed in the tank, measured from the tank bottom; this may be the height of the outlet or the minimum height allowed by a filling control

attributes.name: Maximum water level
attributes.description: Maximum water level allowed in the tank, measured from the tank bottom; this may be the height of the overflow pipe or the maximum height allowed by a filling control

attributes.name: Filling control installed
attributes.description: Control is installed to ensure a desired range of tank fill levels

attributes.name: Type of filling control
attributes.description: Method or device used to maintain the water level in the tank by controlling the influent or effluent flow rate

choices.name: Float valve
choices.description: Flow into the tank is controlled by a gate or plug that is actuated by a float when the water level falls below a certain set point

choices.name: Altitude valve
choices.description: Automatically shuts off flow into an elevated tank when the water level reaches a predetermined level and automatically opens when the pressure in the distribution systems drops below the pressure in the tank

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other fill control method not described in this section

attributes.name: Fill level indicator installed
attributes.description: Device is installed that provides a visual or electronic measurement of the fill level

attributes.name: Power type
attributes.description: Categorization of the power generating device based on design or principles of operation

choices.name: Grid
choices.description: Connection to an electrical transmission and distribution system

choices.name: Generator
choices.description: Diesel, gas, or petrol powered engine that converts rotary motion into electrical current

choices.name: Solar
choices.description: Solar or photovoltaic power system

choices.name: Wind
choices.description: Wind turbine or windmill equipped with an electrical generator

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other power type not defined in this section

attributes.name: Rated power output
attributes.description: Power output that can be sustained for long periods of time; for generators this is the continuous power rating

attributes.name: Maximum power output
attributes.description: Power output that can be provided for short periods of time in response to surges in demand; for generators, sometimes referred to as the standby or intermittent power rating

attributes.name: Nominal voltage
attributes.description: Voltage assigned to a system or circuit of a given voltage class for the purpose of convenient designation; the actual operating voltage may vary above or below this value

attributes.name: Rated voltage
attributes.description: Maximum voltage at which the power system can be operated within thermal and safety limits

attributes.name: Maximum current
attributes.description: Maximum safe current, or starting current, that can be supplied for a short period of time

attributes.name: Type of current
attributes.description: Mode of transmission for electrical current (AC/DC)

choices.name: Single phase AC
choices.description: Alternating current electrical system that uses two wires: one neutral wire and one phase wire in which the voltage rises to a peak in one direction and then reverses to a peak in the opposite direction

choices.name: Three phase AC
choices.description: Alternating current electrical system that uses four wires: one neutral wire and three phase wires in which the voltage rises to a peak and reverses direction at different times

choices.name: DC
choices.description: Direct current system in which current always flows in one direction and the voltage does not change over time

attributes.name: Frequency of current
attributes.description: Frequency at which the voltage rises to a peak, reverses, and rises to a peak again
attributes.applicability: Type of current: Single phase AC, Three phase AC

choices.name: 60 Hz
choices.description: 60 cycles per second

choices.name: 50 Hz
choices.description: 50 cycles per second

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any non-standard current frequency

attributes.name: Generator fuel

choices.name: Gasoline or petrol
choices.description: Fuel made from crude oil and other petroleum liquids that is often used in internal combustion engines

choices.name: Diesel
choices.description: Distillate fuel oil that is used in compression ignition engines

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other fuel used in generators that is not described in this section

attributes.description: Product of the voltage and current provided in an AC power system, which does not account for the reactive power required by inductive loads in the circuit; sometimes referred to by its most common unit of measurement: kVA
attributes.applicability: Type of current: Single phase AC, Three phase AC

attributes.name: Engine cooling system
attributes.description: Type of cooling system used by the generator engine

choices.name: Air
choices.description: Engine cooled by air circulation only

choices.name: Liquid

attributes.name: PV panel type

choices.name: Polycrystalline

choices.name: Monocrystalline
choices.description: Single crystalline or mono panel, made from a single silicon crystal

choices.name: Thin film
choices.description: Thin, flexible panel made from amorphous silicon or other materials

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of photovoltaic panel type not otherwise described in this section

attributes.name: Total number of PV panels
attributes.description: Total number of photovoltaic panels installed in the power system

attributes.name: Treatment type
attributes.description: Categorization of treatment process by treatment method or objective

choices.name: Screen or bar grate
choices.description: Coarse screen or grate that removes large debris from water to prevent clogging of pipes and pumps

choices.name: Filtration
choices.description: Small diameter granular medium, such as sand, removes particulate matter from a liquid stream

choices.name: Membrane filtration
choices.description: Pressurized liquid is forced through a membrane to remove particulate matter

choices.name: Reverse osmosis
choices.description: Pressure-driven membrane removes ions, salts, and other dissolved solids and nonvolatile organics

choices.name: Mixer
choices.description: Agitation or blending process that creates a homogeneous mixture out of two or more components

choices.name: Coagulator
choices.description: Basin in which chemicals (coagulants) are added to destabilize the negative surface charges present in natural particles, allowing them to accumulate

choices.name: Flocculator
choices.description: Device that uses gentle stirring to bring suspended particles together so they will form larger, more separable clumps called floc

choices.name: Clarifier or sedimentation basin
choices.description: Tank or basin in which water is retained to allow settleable matter, such as floc, settle by gravity

choices.name: Chlorination
choices.description: Device or basin that introduces chlorine, in liquid, solid, or gaseous form, for oxidation of organic matter or disinfection

choices.name: Disinfection
choices.description: Process that destroys or inactivates pathogenic organisms by physical or chemical means (use this category for any non-chlorine disinfection methods such as UV or ozone)

choices.name: Aeration
choices.description: Gas transfer process that causes a liquid stream to absorb a gas, such as air or oxygen

choices.name: Air stripping
choices.description: Passing air through liquid to remove volatile compounds

choices.name: Desalinization
choices.description: Process that uses distillation, reverse osmosis, or electrodialysis to remove dissolved mineral salts from seawater or brackish water

choices.name: Solids disposal
choices.description: Process to concentrate, dewater, thicken, or otherwise treat residual solids for safe disposal

choices.name: Chemical feed
choices.description: Addition of chemicals to process water to perform some treatment function, such as pH control or corrosion prevention

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of treatment process not already described in this section

attributes.name: Chlorine type
attributes.description: Chemical form of chlorine used in a treatment process

choices.name: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach)
choices.description: Solution in which sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) is hydrolyzed in water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl); also known as liquid bleach

choices.name: Calcium hypochlorite
choices.description: Dry calcium hypochlorite (Ca(OCl)2) in powder or pellets that can be dissolved in water, where it reacts to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl)

choices.name: Chlorine gas
choices.description: Gaseous molecular chlorine (Cl2) that forms hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and hypochlorite ion (OCl-) when dissolved in water

choices.name: Chloramine
choices.description: Disinfectant produced by mixing chlorine and ammonia (NH3); when added to water, forms mainly monochloramine (NH2Cl) and dichloramine (NHCl2)

choices.name: Chlorine dioxide
choices.description: Red-yellow gas that is very reactive and unstable; decomposes in water to form chlorite ion (ClO2-)

attributes.name: Dosing method
attributes.description: Method used to add chlorine to water to be treated
attributes.applicability: Chlorination type: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach), Calcium hypochlorite, Chloramine

choices.name: Dosing pump
choices.description: Small pump draws concentrated chlorine solution from a tank and adds it to the water stream or tank

choices.name: Drip feed
choices.description: Constant head device, such as a float or bowl, located inside a tank feeds the concentrated chlorine solution at a flow rate that is independent of tank level

choices.name: Constant head aspirator
choices.description: Sealed container with a small outlet tube at the bottom and an air inlet tube at the top that provides a constant pressure and steady flow rate of chlorine solution

choices.name: Gravity feed
choices.description: Tank or bucket that uses gravity to feed a concentrated chlorine solution through a metering orifice or valve that controls the flow rate

choices.name: Batch mixing
choices.description: Chlorine bleach or powder is added to a large tank in batches

choices.name: Tablet or cartridge
choices.description: Water flows through a chamber or cartridge in which chlorine is slowly released from a solid material

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other chlorine dosing method not described in this section

attributes.name: Meter ID
attributes.description: Identification number of code used by the service provider to identify the meter

attributes.name: Meter type
attributes.description: Type of metering performed: bulk metering of the distribution network versus domestic or commercial metering

choices.name: Bulk
choices.description: Used to measure flows throughout the distribution network to monitor performance and detect leaks

choices.name: Domestic
choices.description: Measures flow to a household or private connection

choices.name: Commercial or industrial
choices.description: Measures flow to a commercial or industrial user

choices.name: Production
choices.description: Measures flow from a source or treatment plant

attributes.name: Meter design
attributes.description: Design or operating principle of the meter

choices.name: Turbine
choices.description: Measures flow velocity based on the speed of a rotating turbine

choices.name: Displacement
choices.description: Captures definite volumes of water in a chamber with a piston or disk that discharges the water

choices.name: Ultrasonic
choices.description: Measures flow velocity by transmitting and receiving sound waves that pass diagonally through the flow path

choices.name: Electromagnetic
choices.description: Measures the induced voltage in a sensor that is generated by a fluid as it flows through a pipe

choices.name: Jet
choices.description: One or more jets of water impact on a turbine that measures flow rate

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of meter not otherwise described in this section

attributes.name: Minimum measurable flow rate
attributes.description: Lowest flow rate that can be measured by the meter

attributes.name: Meter measurement type
attributes.description: Type of measurement displayed by the meter (total volume, flow rate, or both)

choices.name: Total volume
choices.description: Totalizing meter, which displays only the total amount of volume that has flowed through the meter, often using a combination of a counter and a sweep hand

choices.name: Flow rate
choices.description: Instantaneous measurement of the current flow rate through the meter

choices.name: Combined
choices.description: Meter display includes both the instantaneous flow rate and the total volume that has flowed through the meter

attributes.name: Electrical type
attributes.description: Type of electrical asset

choices.name: Motor
choices.description: Electromechanical device for converting electrical energy into mechanical energy

choices.name: Actuator
choices.description: Device that uses electrical or pneumatic power to operate valves

choices.name: Power device

choices.name: Electronic
choices.description: Component or device that controls the flow of electrical currents for the purpose of information processing and system control

choices.name: Heater
choices.description: Device that converts electrical energy into heat

choices.name: Blower

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any other type of electrical asset not defined in this section

attributes.name: Electrical power device type

choices.name: Control panel
choices.description: Controls electrical power distribution

choices.name: Circuit breaker
choices.description: Automatic device for stopping the flow of current in a circuit in case of a fault

choices.name: Uninterruptible power supply (UPS)
choices.description: Energy storage device that ensures a constant supply of power, even during power outages

choices.name: Transformer
choices.description: Increases/decreases the voltage/current or visa versa.

choices.name: Power conditioner
choices.description: Device that improves the quality of power delivered by smoothing out voltage spikes and reducing electrical noise

choices.name: Switch
choices.description: Device to disconnect or connect the conducting path in an electrical circuit

choices.name: Motor controller
choices.description: Device for starting, stopping, and regulating the performance and speed of an electric motor

choices.name: Inverter
choices.description: Device for converting direct current into alternating current

attributes.name: Valve type
attributes.description: Purpose or operating principle of a valve

choices.name: Shutoff
choices.description: Closes off the source of water or a section of a distribution system

choices.name: Check
choices.description: Allows flow in only one direction and closes when the flow tries to reverse

choices.name: Backflow preventer
choices.description: Device for preventing backflow of water into a supply system using a double gate, double check, or air gap assembly

choices.name: Washout
choices.description: Valve installed in a low point or depression in a pipeline to allow for drainage of the line; also referred to as a blowoff valve

choices.name: Flow control
choices.description: Pressure-compensating valve installed to regulate the flow of water

choices.name: Pressure reducing
choices.description: Flow valve used to allow water to flow from higher-pressure side to lower-pressure side so as not to exceed a set maximum pressure on the low-pressure side

choices.name: Pressure sustaining
choices.description: Valve that opens only as much as necessary to maintain a certain pressure on the inlet side; also referred to as a back pressure regulator

choices.name: Throttle control
choices.description: Valve installed to reduce the flow through a pipeline

choices.name: Air relief
choices.description: Air valve placed at the summit of a pipeline to release air automatically to prevent air binding and pressure buildup, or to allow air to enter a line if the internal pressure becomes less than atmospheric pressure

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any type of valve not otherwise defined in this section

choices.name: Union
choices.description: Device used to connect two pipes

choices.name: Elbow
choices.description: Fitting that connects two pipes at an angle, usually 90 degrees

choices.name: Tee
choices.description: Fitting in the shape of the letter T that has an opening perpendicular to the main flow pathway, allowing a three-way connection

choices.name: Sleeve

choices.name: Cap
choices.description: Fitting to make the end of a pipe watertight

choices.name: Reducer
choices.description: Fitting used to join two different sized pieces of pipe

choices.name: Cross

choices.name: Inside threaded adapter

choices.name: Other
choices.description: Any type of junction not otherwise described in this section
